derivation:
have hi : iIndepFun (fun (i : S) ω => C i t ω) P :=
  (hind.precomp Subtype.val_injective).comp (fun _ f => f t) (fun _ => measurable_pi_apply t)
simpa using (hi.hasLaw_pi fun i => (hC i).hasLaw_eval t).map_eq
explanation: Mathlib's `iIndepFun.hasLaw_pi` (`HasLaw.lean:256`) states that for a finite index type, if `∀ i, HasLaw (X i) (μ i) P` and the `X i` are independent, then `HasLaw (fun ω i ↦ X i ω) (Measure.pi μ) P`, whose `map_eq` field is exactly `P.map (fun ω i ↦ X i ω) = Measure.pi μ`. The library theorem is this with `ι := S`, `X i := fun ω ↦ C i t ω`, `μ i := gaussianReal 0 t`: the marginals come from `IsPreBrownianReal.hasLaw_eval t` (`X i` has law `gaussianReal 0 t`), and the independence at the fixed time `t` is the restriction of `hind` to the subtype `S` composed with evaluation at `t`. The library instead derives it from `iIndepFun.map_fun_eq_pi_map` plus a `congr 1`/`funext` comparison of the marginals, which is the same argument with `hasLaw_pi` inlined.
